stories.teaser: A plant-based food from local crops to treat child malnutrition
stories.headline: Hebrew University researchers develop a plant-based malnutrition treatment made from locally grown crops
stories.why: Published in Current Developments in Nutrition; promising results in rats, with clinical trials still needed.
texts:
Treating malnutrition with what grows nearby.

Hebrew University researchers led by Dr. Aurélie Bechoff developed ChSMS, a therapeutic food made from chickpea, sorghum, maize and soybean instead of imported powdered milk and peanuts. In a study in rats, it supported better recovery than a commercial formula.

“Access is one of the biggest challenges in treating childhood malnutrition,” says Prof. Efrat Monsonego-Ornan.

#Israel #HebrewUniversity #GlobalHealth #Nutrition

Only about 30% of children who need treatment for severe acute malnutrition receive it.

A Hebrew University team wants to change that with a ready-to-use therapeutic food made from local crops: chickpea, sorghum, maize and soybean. It gets about 14% of its energy from protein, versus 10% for a commercial product, with a protein quality score of 87% versus 69%. The early results come from rats; clinical trials are still needed.

#Israel #HebrewUniversity #GlobalHealth #Nutrition

What if malnutrition treatment didn’t depend on imported milk powder?

Researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem tested a plant-based alternative made from chickpea, sorghum, maize and soybean. In rats, it supported catch-up growth and better recovery than a peanut-and-milk formula. The findings, published in Current Developments in Nutrition, still need confirmation in clinical trials.

#Israel #HebrewUniversity #GlobalHealth #Nutrition
stories.source_name: American Friends of the Hebrew University, Oct 19, 2026
stories.og_title: Could locally grown crops make malnutrition treatment more accessible worldwide?

stories.teaser: A 99-million-year-old insect named after a Teletubbies vacuum cleaner
stories.headline: Tel Aviv University researchers describe “Noo-Noo,” a 99-million-year-old insect with an extraordinary feeding tube
stories.why: A new species found in amber, published in the journal Insects.
texts:
Meet “Noo-Noo.”

Tel Aviv University researchers have described a new planthopper species preserved in amber about 99 million years old. Its mouthparts were nearly twice the length of its body, likely flexible enough to reach sap deep in cracks of tree bark. The name honors the friendly vacuum cleaner from Teletubbies, whose hose looks a lot like it.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Fossils #Science

“This is not merely an insect previously unknown to science, but an animal that developed an evolutionary solution with almost no modern equivalent…” says Dr. Leonidas-Romanos Davranoglou of Tel Aviv University.

His team, led with Dolev Fabrikant, examined 13 amber specimens and used micro-CT scans to reconstruct a feeding tube nearly twice the insect’s body length. Published in the journal Insects.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Fossils #Science

What did insects eat in the age of the dinosaurs?

A Tel Aviv University team found a new species in 99-million-year-old amber, with mouthparts nearly twice its body length. They believe it was a sap-sucking specialist that reached deep into tree bark. They named it Cretodorus noonoo, after the vacuum cleaner from Teletubbies.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Fossils #Science
stories.og_title: Meet “Noo-Noo”: A 99-Million-Year-Old Insect with a Surprising Secret

stories.teaser: Ketamine’s pain relief may not need its mind-altering effect
stories.headline: Tel Aviv University study finds ketamine’s pain relief is separate from its mind-altering effects
stories.why: A brain-imaging study of 37 volunteers, published in Neuropsychopharmacology.
texts:
Pain relief without feeling detached?

Researchers from Tel Aviv University and Tel Aviv Medical Center (Ichilov) found that ketamine’s pain-relieving effect is separate from the dissociation it can cause. In 37 healthy volunteers, stronger dissociation didn’t mean more pain relief. This could point to treatments that keep the relief while reducing the side effects.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #PainRelief #Neuroscience

Does ketamine have to change how you feel to relieve pain? A new Israeli study suggests not.

A team led by Dr. Noam Goldway, with Prof. Talma Hendler and Dr. Haggai Sharon of Tel Aviv University, scanned the brains of 37 volunteers given ketamine and a placebo. Pain relief and dissociation showed up in different brain networks. Published in Neuropsychopharmacology.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #PainRelief #Neuroscience

Two effects, two different brain networks.

Using fMRI scans, Tel Aviv University researchers found that ketamine’s pain relief was linked to reduced activity in the insula and anterior cingulate cortex, while its dissociative effect involved the brain’s default mode network. People with little dissociation could still benefit. The study involved 37 healthy volunteers.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #PainRelief #Neuroscience
stories.og_title: Can Ketamine Relieve Pain Without Altering Consciousness?
